proof:
Context. This child is steps 10-11 of the parent proof. The parent first bounds J(D) = sqrt(det(I + G)) <= sqrt(exp(hsNormSq D)) = exp(hsNormSq D / 2). It then applies this child with s = hsNormSq D and T = n; here 0 <= s, and s <= n when ||D|| <= 1.

1. Put t := s/2. From 0 <= s <= T we get 0 <= t and t <= T/2.
2. Real.add_one_le_exp at -t gives -t + 1 <= exp(-t), i.e. 1 - t <= exp(-t).
3. Multiply step 2 by exp t > 0:
   (1 - t) exp t <= exp(-t) exp t = exp(-t + t) = exp 0 = 1 (Real.exp_add, Real.exp_zero).
   Rearranged: exp t <= 1 + t exp t.
4. exp is monotone and t <= T/2, so exp t <= exp(T/2) (Real.exp_le_exp). Multiplying by t >= 0 gives t exp t <= t exp(T/2).
5. By steps 3 and 4,
   exp(s/2) = exp t <= 1 + t exp(T/2) = 1 + (s/2) exp(T/2) = 1 + (exp(T/2)/2) s. QED

Lean note. Checked against the pinned toolchain: with h2 : (1 - s / 2) * Real.exp (s / 2) ≤ 1 and h4 : s / 2 * Real.exp (s / 2) ≤ s / 2 * Real.exp (T / 2) in context, nlinarith [h2, h4] closes the goal.
key_steps: 1 - t <= exp(-t) for t = s/2 (add_one_le_exp at -t).
Multiplying by exp t > 0 gives exp t <= 1 + t exp t.
t <= T/2 and t >= 0 give t exp t <= t exp(T/2), so exp(s/2) <= 1 + (exp(T/2)/2) s.
